category: PyAEDT & PyEDB: HFSS 3D Layout, EDB, Circuit and Companion Applications
description: The layout-centric and multiphysics side of the Python stack: the Hfss3dLayout class and its Modeler3DLayout (layers, padstacks, nets, components, primitives, ports, extents, meshing, ECAD import, DC IR results), the PyEDB Edb class that edits an .aedb without the GUI (stackup, nets, components, padstacks, ports, cutout, HFSS/SIwave setups, export), the Circuit class and its Nexxim schematic components (dynamic links to HFSS/3D Layout, Touchstone blocks, LNA/Transient setups, push excitations), and the constructors and key methods of the other AEDT applications reachable from the same session (Icepak with EM loss coupling, Maxwell, Q3D/Q2D, EMIT, Mechanical, Twin Builder).

tools.name: Hfss3dLayout (ansys.aedt.core.hfss3dlayout.Hfss3dLayout) constructor and ic_mode
tools.description: Application class for HFSS 3D Layout designs. It takes the same session arguments as Hfss and additionally opens an .aedb folder or an ECAD file (BRD, ODB++, IPC-2581, GDS) directly as a new project, and exposes ic_mode to switch a design between PCB and IC (RaptorX/GDS) editing rules. The object gives access to the layout modeler, ports, setups (HFSS, SIwave DC/AC), differential pairs, extents, meshing options and the same post-processing as Hfss.
tools.usage:
h3d = Hfss3dLayout(project=None, design=None, solution_type=None, setup=None, version=None, non_graphical=False, new_desktop=False,
                   close_on_exit=False, student_version=False, machine="", port=0, aedt_process_id=None, ic_mode=None, remove_lock=False)
h3d.ic_mode          # get/set IC mode
h3d.modeler / h3d.modeler.edb / h3d.post / h3d.setups / h3d.ports / h3d.excitation_names

parameters.name: project
parameters.description: An .aedt file, an .aedb folder (imported as a new project), or a layout file (.brd, .tgz/.zip ODB++, .xml IPC-2581, .gds with control file).

parameters.name: solution_type
parameters.description: Usually None; 3D Layout designs have a single solution type with per-setup solvers.

parameters.name: ic_mode
parameters.description: True/False to force IC or PCB mode when creating the design.

parameters.name: h3d.modeler.edb
parameters.description: A PyEDB Edb object attached to the design's database for low-level edits while the design is open.

tools.example:
from ansys.aedt.core import Hfss3dLayout
h3d = Hfss3dLayout(project="C:/work/board.aedb", version="2025.1", non_graphical=True, new_desktop=True)
print(h3d.design_name, h3d.modeler.model_units)
print(h3d.modeler.layers.all_signal_layers)
print(len(h3d.modeler.components), h3d.modeler.nets.keys() if hasattr(h3d.modeler.nets, 'keys') else '')
h3d.release_desktop()
tools.notes: Opening an .aedb copies it into the new project's folder; edits made through h3d.modeler.edb are written to that copy. Layout designs cannot share a Python object with 3D designs - use separate Hfss / Hfss3dLayout instances on the same project.

tools.name: h3d.modeler (Modeler3DLayout): layers, padstacks, nets, components, pins, geometries, change_net_visibility, fit_all
tools.description: The layout modeler: collections of everything in the layout (components, nets with signal/power split, pins, lines, polygons, rectangles, circles, vias, voids, coordinate systems, clip planes) plus the stackup (layers) and padstack definitions, with helpers to toggle net visibility, run geometry check and fix, merge another design, set temperature dependence and attach Touchstone/SPICE models to components. Each item is an object with editable properties (net, layer, width, position).
tools.usage:
m = h3d.modeler
m.layers / m.stackup / m.padstacks / m.components / m.components_3d / m.nets / m.signal_nets / m.power_nets / m.pins
m.lines / m.polygons / m.rectangles / m.circles / m.vias / m.voids / m.geometries
m.line_names / m.polygon_names / m.via_names / m.rectangle_names / m.circle_names
m.objects_by_layer(layer, object_filter=None, include_voids=False) / m.objects_by_net(net, object_filter=None, include_voids=False)
m.change_net_visibility(assignment=None, visible=False)
m.geometry_check_and_fix_all(min_area=2e-06)
m.set_touchstone_model(assignment, model_path, model_name=None) / m.set_spice_model(assignment, input_file, model_name=None, subcircuit_name=None)
m.set_temperature_dependence(include_temperature_dependence=True, enable_feedback=True, ambient_temp=22, create_project_var=False)
m.merge_design(merged_design=None, pos_x="0.0", pos_y="0.0", rotation="0.0", flip=False)
m.fit_all() / m.model_units / m.edb

parameters.name: components
parameters.description: Dict name -> Components3DLayout with .location, .angle, .placement_layer, .part, .part_type, .pins, .enabled, .change_property().

parameters.name: nets
parameters.description: Dict name -> Nets3DLayout; objects_by_net returns the primitives of a net.

parameters.name: padstacks
parameters.description: Dict of Padstack definitions; new_padstack() creates one for create_via.

parameters.name: lines / polygons / ...
parameters.description: Dicts of Line3dLayout, Polygons3DLayout, Rect3dLayout, Circle3dLayout objects with .net_name, .placement_layer, .points, .lower_left/.upper_right, .set_property().

tools.example:
m = h3d.modeler
m.change_net_visibility(visible=False)
m.change_net_visibility(["DDR_DQ0", "DDR_DQ1", "GND"], visible=True)
for name, comp in m.components.items():
    if comp.part_type in ("Resistor", "Capacitor") and comp.placement_layer == "TOP":
        comp.enabled = False
print(m.objects_by_net("DDR_DQ0"))
m.set_touchstone_model("U2", "C:/models/u2.s8p")
m.geometry_check_and_fix_all()
tools.notes: Native: h3d.oeditor is the layout editor (oEditor for "Layout"); most modeler methods wrap oEditor.CreateLine/CreateRectangle/CreateCircle/CreatePolygon/CreateVia/ChangeProperty. Heavy edits (thousands of primitives) are faster through PyEDB on the closed .aedb.

tools.name: h3d.modeler.layers (Layers): add_layer, stackup layers, signal/dielectric layers, change_stackup_type
tools.description: The Layer Stackup of a 3D Layout or Circuit design: enumerate signal, dielectric and drawing layers, add a layer with type, thickness, elevation and material, read and edit layer properties (material, fill material, thickness, roughness model, etch factor, visibility, colour) through Layer objects, and change the stackup type between Laminate, Overlap and Multizone.
tools.usage:
layers = h3d.modeler.layers
layers.all_layers / layers.all_signal_layers / layers.all_diel_layers / layers.stackup_layers / layers.drawing_layers / layers.zones
layer = layers.add_layer(layer, layer_type="signal", thickness="0mm", elevation="0mm", material="copper", isnegative=False)
layers.layers            # dict id -> Layer (refreshes)
layers.layer_id(name)
layers.change_stackup_type(stackup_type="Multizone", number_zones=3)
layer.name / layer.type / layer.material / layer.fill_material / layer.thickness / layer.lower_elevation / layer.top_bottom / layer.color / layer.is_visible
layer.set_layer_color(r, g, b) / layer.update_stackup_layer()
layers.LengthUnit

parameters.name: layer_type
parameters.description: "signal", "dielectric", "ground"/"conductor" variants as accepted by the stackup editor.

parameters.name: thickness / elevation / material
parameters.description: Unit strings and a material from the project database; dielectrics need a permittivity/loss tangent material.

parameters.name: isnegative
parameters.description: True for negative (etched) layers where drawn geometry is removed from a plane.

parameters.name: stackup_type
parameters.description: "Laminate", "Overlap" or "Multizone" (rigid-flex zones).

tools.example:
layers = h3d.modeler.layers
for l in layers.stackup_layers:
    print(l.name, l.type, l.material, l.thickness, l.lower_elevation)
new = layers.add_layer("L5", layer_type="signal", thickness="0.035mm", material="copper")
diel = layers.add_layer("D5", layer_type="dielectric", thickness="0.2mm", material="FR4_epoxy")
top = layers.layers[layers.layer_id("TOP")]
top.material = "copper"
top.update_stackup_layer()
tools.notes: Native: oEditor.ChangeLayer / AddStackupLayer via the Layer Stackup Editor (Layout > Layers). For bulk stackup edits and import from a CSV/XML, PyEDB's edb.stackup (add_layer, import_stackup, export) is more capable.

tools.name: h3d.modeler.create_line / create_rectangle / create_circle / create_polygon / create_polygon_void / create_via / create_text
tools.description: Draw layout primitives on a layer with a net assignment: trace lines with width and end styles, rectangles and circles, polygons and polygon voids from point lists, vias from an existing padstack between two layers, and text. They return Line3dLayout / Rect3dLayout / Circle3dLayout / Polygons3DLayout objects and are used to build test coupons, add stitching vias, patch a net or create port launch structures.
tools.usage:
line = h3d.modeler.create_line(layer, center_line_coordinates, lw=1, start_style=0, end_style=0, name=None, net=None, **kwargs)
rect = h3d.modeler.create_rectangle(layer, origin, dimensions, corner_radius=0, angle=0, name=None, net=None, **kwargs)
circ = h3d.modeler.create_circle(layer, x, y, radius, name=None, net=None, **kwargs)
poly = h3d.modeler.create_polygon(layer, point_list, name=None, net=None, **kwargs)
void = h3d.modeler.create_polygon_void(layer, point_list, assignment, name=None, **kwargs)
via = h3d.modeler.create_via(padstack="PlanarEMVia", x=0, y=0, rotation=0, hole_diam=None, top_layer=None, bot_layer=None, name=None, net=None)
txt = h3d.modeler.create_text(text, position, angle=0, font_size=12)
h3d.modeler.new_padstack(name="Padstack")     # Padstack object: add_layer(), padstack hole/pad definitions, create()

parameters.name: layer / net
parameters.description: Layer name and net name; a missing net is created.

parameters.name: center_line_coordinates / point_list
parameters.description: [[x, y], [x, y], ...] in model units or unit strings/variables.

parameters.name: lw / start_style / end_style
parameters.description: Line width and end styles 0 = Flat, 1 = Extended, 2 = Round.

parameters.name: padstack / top_layer / bot_layer / hole_diam
parameters.description: Padstack definition name, span and optional hole override for create_via.

tools.example:
h3d["w"] = "0.2mm"
trace = h3d.modeler.create_line("TOP", [[0, 0], [10, 0], [10, 5]], lw="w", name="Trace1", net="SIG1")
gnd = h3d.modeler.create_rectangle("GND", [-2, -2], [14, 9], name="GndPlane", net="GND")
ps = h3d.modeler.new_padstack("Via_0p3")
ps.add_layer("TOP", pad_hole=0.3, pad_diameter=0.6)
ps.add_layer("GND", pad_hole=0.3, pad_diameter=0.6)
ps.create()
for x in range(0, 12, 2):
    h3d.modeler.create_via("Via_0p3", x=x, y=-1, top_layer="TOP", bot_layer="GND", net="GND")
tools.notes: Native: oEditor.CreateLine(["NAME:Contents", "lineGeometry:=", ["Name:=", "line_0", "LayerName:=", "TOP", "lw:=", "0.2mm", "endstyle:=", 0, "StartCap:=", 0, "n:=", 3, "U:=", "mm", "x:=", 0, "y:=", 0, ...]]) and similar CreateRectangle/CreateCircle/CreatePolygon/CreateVia calls. Coordinates default to the layout units (h3d.modeler.model_units).

tools.name: h3d.create_edge_port / h3d.create_wave_port (edge-based ports in 3D Layout)
tools.description: Ports on the edge of a trace or polygon: create_edge_port makes a gap (lumped) port by default, a circuit port (with an optional reference primitive/edge for the negative terminal) or a wave port with horizontal/vertical extension factors and a PEC launcher; create_wave_port is the dedicated wave-port form. Edge ports are how transmission-line coupons, connectors at the board edge and de-embedded launches are excited in layout designs.
tools.usage:
port = h3d.create_edge_port(assignment, edge_number, is_circuit_port=False, is_wave_port=False, wave_horizontal_extension=5,
                            wave_vertical_extension=3, wave_launcher="1mm", reference_primitive=None, reference_edge_number=0)
port = h3d.create_wave_port(assignment, edge_number, wave_horizontal_extension=5, wave_vertical_extension=3, wave_launcher="1mm")
h3d.delete_port(name, remove_geometry=False)
h3d.ports / h3d.port_list / h3d.excitation_names

parameters.name: assignment / edge_number
parameters.description: Primitive name (or Line3dLayout) and the index of its edge; for a line 0 and 1 are the two ends.

parameters.name: is_circuit_port / reference_primitive / reference_edge_number
parameters.description: Circuit port between the edge and a reference edge on another primitive.

parameters.name: is_wave_port / wave_horizontal_extension / wave_vertical_extension / wave_launcher
parameters.description: Wave port sized as multiples of the trace width/height with a PEC launcher length.

parameters.name: BoundaryObject3dLayout
parameters.description: Returned port with .name, .props (e.g. "Impedance", "Renormalize", "DeembedDist"), .update(), .delete().

tools.example:
p1 = h3d.create_edge_port("Trace1", 0, is_wave_port=True, wave_horizontal_extension=6, wave_vertical_extension=4, wave_launcher="0.5mm")
p2 = h3d.create_edge_port("Trace1", 1)                       # gap port at the other end
p2.props["Impedance"] = "50ohm"
p2.update()
print(h3d.port_list)
tools.notes: Native: oEditor.CreateEdgePort(["NAME:Contents", "edge:=", ["et:=", "pe", "prim:=", "Trace1", "edge:=", 0], "circuit:=", False, "btype:=", 0]) followed by oModule("Excitations").SetWavePort / EditPort. Wave ports in layout need the extents to include the launcher; check edit_hfss_extents.

tools.name: h3d.create_coax_port / h3d.create_pin_port / h3d.create_ports_by_nets / h3d.create_ports_on_component_by_nets / create_pec_on_component_by_nets
tools.description: Vertical and component ports in 3D Layout: a coax port on a via (with radial extent and reference layer), a pin port at coordinates spanning two layers, automatic port creation on every pin of the given nets or on the pins of one component (the Auto Port on Nets workflow used for DDR/SerDes extraction), and PEC shorting of a component's pins on selected nets (for decoupling capacitor idealisation).
tools.usage:
port = h3d.create_coax_port(via, radial_extent=0.1, layer=None, alignment="lower")
port = h3d.create_pin_port(name, x=0, y=0, rotation=0, top_layer=None, bottom_layer=None)
ports = h3d.create_ports_by_nets(nets)
ports = h3d.create_ports_on_component_by_nets(component, nets)
h3d.create_pec_on_component_by_nets(component, nets)

parameters.name: via
parameters.description: Via primitive name for the coax port.

parameters.name: radial_extent / layer / alignment
parameters.description: Coax outer radius factor, reference layer, and "lower"/"upper" alignment of the port on that layer.

parameters.name: x / y / rotation / top_layer / bottom_layer
parameters.description: Pin port location and span.

parameters.name: nets / component
parameters.description: Net name(s) and component reference designator ("U1").

parameters.name: return
parameters.description: BoundaryObject3dLayout or a list of them.

tools.example:
ports = h3d.create_ports_on_component_by_nets("U1", ["DDR_DQ0", "DDR_DQ1", "DDR_DQS_P", "DDR_DQS_N"])
ports += h3d.create_ports_on_component_by_nets("U2", ["DDR_DQ0", "DDR_DQ1", "DDR_DQS_P", "DDR_DQS_N"])
h3d.create_pec_on_component_by_nets("C12", ["VDD", "GND"])
cp = h3d.create_coax_port("via_123", radial_extent=0.15, layer="BOTTOM")
print([p.name for p in ports])
tools.notes: Ports created on component pins are circuit ports referenced to the nearest ground; their names combine component and pin. For fully controlled port creation (reference designator, terminal type, impedance, solder-ball models) use PyEDB's edb.components.create_port_on_component / edb.excitation_manager before opening the layout.

tools.name: h3d.create_setup (HFSS 3D Layout setup properties) / Setup3DLayout / SweepHFSS3DLayout
tools.description: Create a 3D Layout analysis setup and its sweeps. The HFSS setup template exposes the layout-specific options - adaptive frequency and Max Delta S, Phi/PhiPlus/Classic mesher, mesh size factor, lambda and quality refinement, causal materials, solver type, accuracy level, minimum triangle angle, number of processors - and SIwave DC IR / SIwave SYZ setups are created for the SIwave solvers embedded in 3D Layout. Sweeps use SweepHFSS3DLayout with the same range properties as HFSS.
tools.usage:
setup = h3d.create_setup(name="MySetupAuto", setup_type=None, **kwargs)     # HFSS setup by default
setup.props["AdaptiveSettings"]["SingleFrequencyDataList"]["AdaptiveFrequencyData"]["AdaptiveFrequency"] = "5GHz"
setup.props["AdaptiveSettings"]["SingleFrequencyDataList"]["AdaptiveFrequencyData"]["MaxDelta"] = "0.01"
setup.props["AdvancedSettings"]["MeshSizeFactor"] = 2
setup.update()
sweep = h3d.create_linear_count_sweep(setup, unit="GHz", start_frequency=0.1, stop_frequency=20, num_of_freq_points=2001, name=None, save_fields=False, save_rad_fields_only=False, sweep_type="Interpolating", interpolation_tol_percent=0.5, interpolation_max_solutions=250, use_q3d_for_dc=False)
sweep = h3d.create_linear_step_sweep(setup, unit="GHz", start_frequency=0.1, stop_frequency=20, step_size=0.01, ...)
sweep = h3d.create_single_point_sweep(setup, unit="GHz", freq=5, ...)
h3d.analyze(setup=None, cores=None, tasks=None, gpus=None, ...)
h3d.get_setup(name) / h3d.setups / h3d.delete_setup(name)

parameters.name: kwargs
parameters.description: Setup template keys in nested dict form, e.g. SingleFrequencyDataList__AdaptiveFrequency="5GHz", MeshSizeFactor=2, ViaNumSides, ViaMaterial, and for SIwave setups DC/AC settings such as DCSliderPos, ThermalFeedback, MeshResolution.

parameters.name: sweep_type
parameters.description: "Interpolating", "Discrete", "Fast".

parameters.name: use_q3d_for_dc
parameters.description: Compute the DC point with the Q3D DC solver for accurate low-frequency extrapolation.

tools.example:
setup = h3d.create_setup("HFSS_10G", SingleFrequencyDataList__AdaptiveFrequency="10GHz", MeshSizeFactor=1.5)
setup.props["AdvancedSettings"]["UseCausalMaterials"] = True
setup.update()
sw = h3d.create_linear_count_sweep("HFSS_10G", "GHz", 0.01, 20, 2000, name="Sweep1", sweep_type="Interpolating", use_q3d_for_dc=True)
h3d.analyze("HFSS_10G", cores=16)
h3d.export_touchstone(setup="HFSS_10G", sweep="Sweep1", output_file="C:/work/ddr.s8p")
tools.notes: Native: oModule = oDesign.GetModule("SolveSetups"); oModule.Add(["NAME:HFSS_10G", "SolveSetupType:=", "HFSS", ["NAME:Properties", ...], ["NAME:AdaptiveSettings", ...]]) and oModule.AddSweep(setup, [...]). SIwave setups are added with SolveSetupType "SIwaveDCIR" / "SIwave"; the exact property names are in the PyAEDT SetupTemplates3DLayout page and are best captured by recording.

tools.name: h3d.import_gds / import_brd / import_odb / import_ipc2581 / import_gerber / import_dxf / import_awr / import_edb
tools.description: ECAD import into a new 3D Layout project: GDSII with an XML/TECH control file mapping GDS layers to a stackup, Cadence .brd, ODB++ archives (.tgz/.zip), IPC-2581 XML, Gerber sets, DXF, AWR Microwave Office files and existing .aedb folders. Each import creates an .aedb, opens it as a new project (optionally replacing the active one) and returns True; the translators require the corresponding ECAD import license features.
tools.usage:
h3d.import_gds(input_file, output_dir=None, control_file=None, set_as_active=True, close_active_project=False)
h3d.import_brd(input_file, output_dir=None, set_as_active=True, close_active_project=False)
h3d.import_odb(input_file, output_dir=None, set_as_active=True, close_active_project=False)
h3d.import_ipc2581(input_file, output_dir=None, set_as_active=True, close_active_project=False)
h3d.import_gerber(input_file, output_dir=None, set_as_active=True, close_active_project=False)
h3d.import_dxf(input_file, output_dir=None, set_as_active=True, close_active_project=False)
h3d.import_awr(input_file, output_dir=None, set_as_active=True, close_active_project=False)
h3d.import_edb(input_folder)

parameters.name: input_file
parameters.description: Path to the ECAD file/archive; for Gerber the zipped set or the job file.

parameters.name: output_dir
parameters.description: Destination .aedb folder; default next to the input.

parameters.name: control_file
parameters.description: GDS import XML or .tech file describing layers, materials, vias and options (also used by PyEDB's import_gds_file).

parameters.name: set_as_active / close_active_project
parameters.description: Activate the imported project and optionally close the previous one.

tools.example:
h3d = Hfss3dLayout(version="2025.1", non_graphical=True)
h3d.import_ipc2581("C:/ecad/board.xml", output_dir="C:/work/board.aedb")
h3d.import_gds("C:/ecad/chip.gds", output_dir="C:/work/chip.aedb", control_file="C:/ecad/chip_stackup.xml")
print(h3d.project_name, h3d.modeler.layers.all_signal_layers)
tools.notes: GUI: File > Import > ECAD (Cadence, Mentor, Altium, Zuken translators through ODB++/IPC-2581/ANF) or Layout > Import GDSII with the technology mapping dialog. The Layout Design Toolkit and PyEDB's Edb(edbpath=<layout file>) offer the same imports without the desktop.

tools.name: h3d.edit_hfss_extents / h3d.set_meshing_settings / h3d.show_extent
tools.description: Solver-region and meshing controls of a layout design: the dielectric and air-box extents (bounding box, conformal, convex hull or polygon, with horizontal and vertical paddings and truncation at a ground layer) that define the 3D volume HFSS builds from the 2.5D layout, the mesh method (Phi, Phi Plus, Classic) with intersection checks and fallback, and a toggle to display the extent outline.
tools.usage:
h3d.edit_hfss_extents(diel_extent_type=None, diel_extent_horizontal_padding=None, diel_honor_primitives_on_diel_layers="keep", air_extent_type=None,
                      air_truncate_model_at_ground_layer="keep", air_vertical_positive_padding=None, air_vertical_negative_padding=None,
                      airbox_values_as_dim=True, air_horizontal_padding=None, diel_extent_polygon=None, air_extent_polygon=None)
h3d.set_meshing_settings(mesh_method="Phi", enable_intersections_check=True, use_alternative_fallback=True)
h3d.show_extent(show=True)
h3d.enable_rigid_flex()

parameters.name: diel_extent_type / air_extent_type
parameters.description: "BboxExtent", "ConformalExtent", "ConvexHullExtent" or "PolygonExtent" (with *_extent_polygon).

parameters.name: *_padding
parameters.description: Percent strings ("0.1" = 10 %) or absolute lengths when airbox_values_as_dim is True.

parameters.name: air_truncate_model_at_ground_layer
parameters.description: "true"/"false"/"keep" - stop the air box at the ground plane instead of enclosing the whole stack.

parameters.name: mesh_method
parameters.description: "Phi" (layered mesher, default), "PhiPlus" (handles arbitrary via/trace geometry), "Classic".

tools.example:
h3d.edit_hfss_extents(diel_extent_type="ConformalExtent", diel_extent_horizontal_padding="0.05",
                      air_extent_type="BboxExtent", air_vertical_positive_padding="5mm", air_vertical_negative_padding="0mm",
                      air_truncate_model_at_ground_layer="true", airbox_values_as_dim=True)
h3d.set_meshing_settings("PhiPlus")
h3d.show_extent(True)
tools.notes: Native: oDesign.GetModule("SolveSetups") / oEditor.SetHfssExtents([...]) and oDesign.DesignOptions([...]) for the mesher. Truncating at ground is the usual choice for boards with a solid reference plane; radiating structures need a full air box with a radiation boundary (HFSS 3D Layout adds it automatically at the extents).

tools.name: h3d.get_dcir_solution_data / get_dcir_element_data_via / get_dcir_element_data_loop_resistance / get_dcir_element_data_current_source
tools.description: Retrieve SIwave DC IR results solved inside a 3D Layout design as SolutionData: per-element tables for sources, RL elements, vias, bondwires and probes (voltage, current, power, loop resistance, position, limits, IR drop), and dedicated helpers for via currents, loop resistances and current-source data. They power automated PDN sign-off scripts (max via current, IR drop at sinks) without opening the DC IR report tables.
tools.usage:
data = h3d.get_dcir_solution_data(setup, show="RL", category="Loop_Resistance")
vias = h3d.get_dcir_element_data_via(setup)
loop = h3d.get_dcir_element_data_loop_resistance(setup)
src = h3d.get_dcir_element_data_current_source(setup)

parameters.name: setup
parameters.description: Name of the SIwave DC IR setup.

parameters.name: show
parameters.description: "Sources", "RL", "Vias", "Bondwires" or "Probes".

parameters.name: category
parameters.description: "Voltage", "Current", "Power", "Loop_Resistance", "Resistance", "Inductance", "X", "Y", "Limit", "IR Drop".

tools.example:
dc = h3d.create_setup("DCIR1", setup_type="SiwaveDC3DLayout") if False else h3d.get_setup("DCIR1")

tools.name: Edb (pyedb.Edb) constructor, save/save_as/close, context manager
tools.description: PyEDB's main class opens an Electronics Database folder (.aedb) - or imports a layout file into a new one - without launching AEDT, giving direct programmatic access to the layout: stackup, materials, nets, components, padstacks, primitives, ports and sources, cutouts, simulation setups and exports. Edits are committed with save()/save_as() and the database released with close(), which the context manager does automatically.

from pyedb import Edb

edb.save() / edb.save_as(path) / edb.close()

from pyedb import Edb

This is where board stackups are corrected before any solve.
tools.usage:
edb.stackup.layers / edb.stackup.signal_layers / edb.stackup.dielectric_layers / edb.stackup.stackup_layers / edb.stackup.layer_types

edb.materials.add_conductor_material(name, conductivity) / add_dielectric_material(name, permittivity, dielectric_loss_tangent)

parameters.name: method / base_layer
parameters.description: "add_on_top", "add_on_bottom", "add_below", "add_above" relative to base_layer, or "insert_below"/"insert_above".

parameters.name: layer_type
parameters.description: "signal" or "dielectric".

parameters.name: assign_roughness_model
parameters.description: "huray" or "groisse" on "top", "bottom", "side" or "all" surfaces of a signal layer.

edb.materials.add_djordjevicsarkar_dielectric("Megtron6", 3.4, 0.002, 10e9)
for name, layer in edb.stackup.dielectric_layers.items():
    layer.material = "Megtron6"
for name, layer in edb.stackup.signal_layers.items():

tools.name: edb.cutout (net-based cutout with extent types) / edb.layout_validation
tools.description: Reduce a board to the region around selected signal nets with their reference nets: cutout clips the layout to a conforming, convex-hull or bounding-box extent grown by an expansion size, keeps or removes single-pin components and ports, optionally uses the PyAEDT (Python-side) clipping for speed, and can create a new EDB for the result. layout_validation offers checks and fixes (disjoint nets, illegal net names, self-intersecting polygons, dc shorts) typically run before a cutout or a solve.
tools.usage:
poly = edb.cutout(signal_list=None, reference_list=None, extent_type="ConvexHull", expansion_size=0.002, use_round_corner=False,
                  output_aedb_path=None, open_cutout_at_end=True, use_pyaedt_cutout=True, number_of_threads=4, use_pyaedt_extent_computing=True,
                  extent_defeature=0, remove_single_pin_components=False, custom_extent=None, custom_extent_units="mm", include_partial_instances=False,
                  keep_voids=True, check_terminals=False, include_pingroups=False, expansion_factor=0, maximum_iterations=10, preserve_components_with_model=False,
                  simple_pad_check=True, keep_lines_as_path=False, include_voids_in_extents=False)
edb.layout_validation.dc_shorts(net_list=None, fix=False)
edb.layout_validation.disjoint_nets(net_list=None, keep_only_main_net=False, clean_disjoints_less_than=0.0, order_by_area=False, keep_disjoint_pins=False)
edb.layout_validation.fix_self_intersections(net_list=None)
edb.layout_validation.illegal_net_names(fix=False) / illegal_rlc_values(fix=False) / padstacks_no_name(fix=False)

parameters.name: signal_list / reference_list
parameters.description: Nets to keep entirely and reference (ground/power) nets to keep only inside the extent.

parameters.name: extent_type
parameters.description: "Conforming", "ConvexHull" or "Bounding".

parameters.name: expansion_size
parameters.description: Distance (metres, or unit string) the extent is grown around the signal nets.

parameters.name: output_aedb_path / open_cutout_at_end
parameters.description: Write the cutout as a new .aedb and switch the Edb object to it.

parameters.name: custom_extent
parameters.description: Explicit polygon [[x,y],...] to clip to instead of a computed extent.

parameters.name: remove_single_pin_components
parameters.description: Drop components left with one pin after clipping.

tools.example:
edb.layout_validation.disjoint_nets(["GND"])
edb.cutout(signal_list=["DDR_DQ0", "DDR_DQ1", "DDR_DQS_P", "DDR_DQS_N"], reference_list=["GND", "VDDQ"],
           extent_type="ConvexHull", expansion_size="3mm", use_round_corner=True,
           output_aedb_path="C:/work/ddr_cutout.aedb", open_cutout_at_end=True, remove_single_pin_components=True)
print(edb.get_statistics())
edb.save()
tools.notes: Cutouts drastically reduce HFSS solve size; expansion of a few mm beyond the traces is typical for stripline, more for microstrip. The Cutout extension in the Extension Manager wraps this call. Legacy names: create_cutout / create_cutout_multithread.

tools.name: edb.create_hfss_setup / create_siwave_syz_setup / create_siwave_dc_setup / edb.setups
tools.description: Define simulation setups inside the EDB so a layout arrives in AEDT ready to solve: an HFSS setup (adaptive frequency, Max Delta S, passes, mesh operations, sweeps with types and ranges, causal materials, via modelling), a SIwave SYZ (AC) setup with its accuracy/mesh options and sweeps, and a SIwave DC IR setup (DC slider, thermal feedback, mesh resolution, contact resistance). The setup objects expose add_sweep / add_frequency_sweep, adaptive settings and advanced settings.
tools.usage:
setup = edb.create_hfss_setup(name=None)
setup.set_solution_single_frequency(frequency="5GHz", max_num_passes=10, max_delta_s="0.02")
setup.set_solution_multi_frequencies(frequencies=("5GHz", "10GHz"), max_num_passes=10, max_delta_s="0.02")
setup.set_solution_broadband(low_frequency="5GHz", high_frequency="10GHz", max_num_passes=10, max_delta_s="0.02")
sweep = setup.add_sweep(name=None, frequency_set=None, **kwargs)     # frequency_set e.g. [["linear count", "0GHz", "20GHz", 2001]]
setup.hfss_solver_settings.enhanced_low_freq_accuracy = True; setup.hfss_solver_settings.order_basis = "first"
setup.add_length_mesh_operation({"GND": ["TOP", "BOTTOM"]}, "mop1", max_elements=1000, max_length="1mm")
syz = edb.create_siwave_syz_setup(name=None, **kwargs)
syz.add_sweep(name=None, frequency_set=None, **kwargs)
dc = edb.create_siwave_dc_setup(name=None, **kwargs)
dc.dc_settings.compute_inductance = True; dc.dc_settings.dc_slider_position = 1
edb.setups / edb.simulation_setups / edb.hfss_setups / edb.siwave_ac_setups / edb.siwave_dc_setups

parameters.name: frequency_set
parameters.description: List of [type, start, stop, count/step] rows, types "linear count", "linear scale", "log scale", "single points".

parameters.name: hfss_solver_settings
parameters.description: Order of basis, enhanced low-frequency accuracy, solver type, relative residual, use Shell elements.

parameters.name: adaptive_settings
parameters.description: Adaptive type (single/multi/broadband), max passes, delta S, min converged passes, save fields.

parameters.name: dc_settings / dc_advanced_settings
parameters.description: SIwave DC IR options: slider position (0-2), compute inductance, contact resistance, mesh bondwires, refine vias, percent local refinement.

tools.example:
setup = edb.create_hfss_setup("HFSS_DDR")
setup.set_solution_single_frequency("5GHz", max_num_passes=15, max_delta_s="0.01")
setup.hfss_solver_settings.enhanced_low_freq_accuracy = True
setup.add_sweep("Sweep1", frequency_set=[["linear count", "0GHz", "20GHz", 2001]])
dc = edb.create_siwave_dc_setup("DCIR")
dc.dc_settings.dc_slider_position = 2
edb.save(); edb.close()

from ansys.aedt.core import Hfss3dLayout
h3d = Hfss3dLayout(project="C:/work/ddr_cutout.aedb", version="2025.1", non_graphical=True)
h3d.analyze("HFSS_DDR", cores=16)
tools.notes: Sources and sinks for DC IR are created with edb.siwave.create_voltage_source_on_pin / create_current_source_on_pin (or on nets/pin groups) and edb.siwave.create_voltage_probe; ports for HFSS with edb.excitation_manager / edb.hfss.create_wave_port / create_edge_port. edb.solve_siwave() runs SIwave in batch from PyEDB; edb.export_hfss/export_q3d/export_maxwell write 3D projects.

tools.name: edb.configuration (JSON/TOML configure layout: stackup, components, ports, setups, sweeps in one file) / edb.export_to_ipc2581 / import_layout_file
tools.description: The declarative front end of PyEDB: a JSON or TOML configuration file describes everything to apply to a layout - stackup and materials, component values and models, solder balls, pin groups, ports and sources, differential pairs, cutout, HFSS/SIwave setups and sweeps, operations such as via removal - and edb.configuration.load + run applies it in one pass (the Configure Layout extension is its GUI). import_layout_file translates ECAD into the EDB and export_to_ipc2581 writes the layout back out as IPC-2581 XML for tools that read it.
tools.usage:
edb.configuration.load(config_file, append=True, apply_file=False, output_file=None, open_at_the_end=True)
edb.configuration.run()
edb.configuration.export(file_path, stackup=True, package_definitions=False, setups=True, sources=True, ports=True, nets=True, pin_groups=True, operations=True, components=True, boundaries=True, s_parameters=True, padstacks=True, general=True)
edb.import_layout_file(input_file, working_dir=None, anstranslator_full_path="", use_ppe=False, control_file=None, tech_file=None, map_file=None, layer_filter=None)
edb.export_to_ipc2581(ipc_path=None, units="MILLIMETER")
edb.export_hfss(path, net_list=None, num_cores=None, aedt_file_name=None, hidden=False) / edb.export_q3d(...) / edb.export_maxwell(...)

parameters.name: config_file
parameters.description: Path to the JSON/TOML; sections: general, stackup, components, padstacks, pin_groups, ports, sources, setups, sweeps? (inside setups), operations (cutout, delete/replace), s_parameters, nets, boundaries.

parameters.name: append / apply_file
parameters.description: Merge with a loaded configuration and apply immediately.

parameters.name: export(...)
parameters.description: Dump the current EDB state to a configuration file - the starting point for a template.

tools.notes: The configuration schema is versioned with PyEDB; export() from a configured board gives a valid template for the installed version. The same JSON drives the 'Configure Layout' extension in the AEDT ribbon.

tools.name: Circuit (ansys.aedt.core.circuit.Circuit) constructor / circuit.modeler.schematic (NexximComponents)
tools.description: The Circuit (Nexxim) application class shares the AEDT session and project with Hfss and exposes the schematic editor through circuit.modeler.schematic, a NexximComponents object that places and wires components: passives (create_resistor, create_inductor, create_capacitor, create_coupling_inductors), sources and probes, transistors and diodes, ports, library parts, Touchstone/state-space blocks, SPICE sub-circuits and dynamic links to EM designs. Components are CircuitComponent objects with pins, location, parameters and properties.
tools.usage:
cir = Circuit(project=None, design=None, solution_type=None, setup=None, version=None, non_graphical=False, new_desktop=False, close_on_exit=False, student_version=False, machine="", port=0, aedt_process_id=None, remove_lock=False)
sch = cir.modeler.schematic
r = sch.create_resistor(name=None, value=50, location=None, angle=0, use_instance_id_netlist=False)
l = sch.create_inductor(name=None, value=1e-9, location=None, angle=0, ...)
c = sch.create_capacitor(name=None, value=1e-12, location=None, angle=0, ...)
sch.create_gnd(location=None, angle=0, page=1)
sch.create_voltage_dc(...) / create_voltage_pulse(...) / create_voltage_pwl(...) / create_current_dc(...) / create_voltage_probe(...) / create_current_probe(...)
sch.create_npn(...) / create_pnp(...) / create_diode(...)
sch.create_component(name=None, component_library="Resistors", component_name="RES_", location=None, angle=0, use_instance_id_netlist=False, global_netlist_list=None, page=1, flip=False)
sch.create_wire(points, name="", page=1) / sch.connect_components_in_series(assignment, use_wire=True) / connect_components_in_parallel(assignment)
sch.create_page_port(name, location=None, angle=0, page=1) / sch.create_interface_port(name, location=None, angle=0, page=1)
comp.pins / comp.location / comp.angle / comp.parameters / comp.set_property(name, value) / comp.delete()
sch.components / sch.get_component(name) / sch.wires / sch.refresh_all_ids()

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: Element value in SI (50, 1e-9) or with units ("50ohm", "1nH").

parameters.name: location / angle / page
parameters.description: Schematic position in mils, rotation in degrees, schematic page.

parameters.name: component_library / component_name
parameters.description: Library path and part name as in the Component Libraries tree (e.g. "Nexxim Circuit Elements\\Distributed", "TRLK").

parameters.name: CircuitComponent.pins
parameters.description: CircuitPins with .connect_to_component(other_pins) and .location for wiring.

tools.example:
from ansys.aedt.core import Circuit
cir = Circuit(design="Match", version="2025.1")
sch = cir.modeler.schematic
p1 = sch.create_interface_port("P1", location=[-1000, 0])
l1 = sch.create_inductor("L1", "3.2nH", location=[-500, 0])
c1 = sch.create_capacitor("C1", "1.5pF", location=[0, -300], angle=90)
p2 = sch.create_interface_port("P2", location=[500, 0])
gnd = sch.create_gnd(location=[0, -700])
p1.pins[0].connect_to_component(l1.pins[0])
l1.pins[1].connect_to_component([c1.pins[0], p2.pins[0]])
c1.pins[1].connect_to_component(gnd.pins[0])
setup = cir.create_setup("LNA1", setup_type="NexximLNA", Data="LINC 1GHz 3GHz 201")
cir.analyze()
cir.post.create_report("dB(S(P1,P1))")
tools.notes: Native: oEditor = oDesign.SetActiveEditor("SchematicEditor"); oEditor.CreateComponent(["NAME:ComponentProps", "Name:=", "Nexxim Circuit Elements\\Resistors:RES_", "Id:=", "1"], ["NAME:Attributes", "Page:=", 1, "X:=", 0, "Y:=", 0, "Angle:=", 0, "Flip:=", False]) and oEditor.CreateWire. Component locations use the schematic grid units; interface ports become the S-parameter port names.

tools.name: schematic.add_subcircuit_dynamic_link / add_subcircuit_3dlayout / create_touchstone_component / create_component_from_spicemodel / create_field_model
tools.description: Bring EM and model data into a schematic: add_subcircuit_dynamic_link places a dynamically linked HFSS, Q3D or 2D Extractor design (solved on demand, variables shared), add_subcircuit_3dlayout places an HFSS 3D Layout design, create_touchstone_component adds an N-port block from an .sNp file (creating the model definition if needed), create_component_from_spicemodel imports a SPICE .lib/.sp sub-circuit, and create_field_model links a Maxwell/other field design. These are the building blocks of the HFSS-to-Circuit co-simulation flow.
tools.usage:
comp = sch.add_subcircuit_dynamic_link(pyaedt_app=None, solution_name=None, extrusion_length=None, enable_cable_modeling=True, default_matrix="Original", tline_port="", name=None)
comp = sch.add_subcircuit_3dlayout(name)
comp = sch.create_touchstone_component(model_name, location=None, angle=0, show_bitmap=True, page=1, image_path=None)
comp = sch.create_component_from_spicemodel(input_file, model=None, create_component=True, location=None, symbol_path="Nexxim Circuit Elements\\Nexxim_symbols:", symbol="", page=1)
comp = sch.create_field_model(design_name, solution_name, pin_names, model_type="hfss", posx=0, posy=1, ...)
sch.set_sim_solution_on_hfss_subcircuit(component, solution_name="Setup1 : Sweep") / sch.set_sim_option_on_hfss_subcircuit(component, option="simulate")
sch.refresh_dynamic_link(name)
sch.add_siwave_dynamic_link(...) / sch.add_q3d_rlgc(pyaedt_app, ...)

parameters.name: pyaedt_app
parameters.description: An Hfss, Hfss3dLayout, Q3d or Q2d object of a design in the same project.

parameters.name: solution_name
parameters.description: "Setup1 : Sweep1" of the linked design used for the S-matrix.

parameters.name: tline_port / extrusion_length / enable_cable_modeling
parameters.description: 2D-extractor / Q2D specifics: transmission-line port, extrusion length and cable modelling.

parameters.name: model_name
parameters.description: Existing Touchstone model name or a file path (the model is created from the file).

parameters.name: option (set_sim_option_on_hfss_subcircuit)
parameters.description: "simulate" (solve the EM design when missing) or "interpolate".

tools.example:
hfss = Hfss(design="Filter")
cir = Circuit(design="FilterCircuit")
sch = cir.modeler.schematic
filt = sch.add_subcircuit_dynamic_link(hfss, solution_name="Setup1 : Sweep1", name="HFSS_Filter")
sch.set_sim_option_on_hfss_subcircuit(filt, "simulate")
amp = sch.create_touchstone_component("C:/models/lna.s2p", location=[1500, 0])
p1 = sch.create_interface_port("In", [-1500, 0]); p2 = sch.create_interface_port("Out", [3000, 0])
p1.pins[0].connect_to_component(filt.pins[0]); filt.pins[1].connect_to_component(amp.pins[0]); amp.pins[1].connect_to_component(p2.pins[0])
cir.create_setup("LNA", setup_type="NexximLNA", Data="LINC 1GHz 3GHz 401")
cir.analyze()
tools.notes: Dynamic links keep the EM design's variables in the circuit (tunable); changing them triggers an EM re-solve unless interpolation is enabled. GUI: Circuit > Draw > Add Sub-circuit > HFSS / 3D Layout design, and Add Model > Touchstone.

tools.name: circuit.create_setup (NexximLNA / NexximDC / NexximTransient / NexximQEye / NexximVEye / NexximAMI) / SetupCircuit
tools.description: Nexxim analysis setups: linear network analysis (LNA) with a frequency list, DC operating point, transient with stop time and step, quick-eye and verification-eye analyses for SerDes channels, and IBIS-AMI simulations. The Data string uses Nexxim sweep syntax (LINC/LIN/DEC), and the returned SetupCircuit exposes props (e.g. TransientData, UseCache) and add_sweep_points / add_sweep_step / add_sweep_count for sweep definitions.
tools.usage:
setup = cir.create_setup(name="MySetupAuto", setup_type=None, **kwargs)     # None = NexximLNA
from ansys.aedt.core.generic.constants import Setups
lna = cir.create_setup("LNA1", Setups.NexximLNA, Data="LINC 1GHz 10GHz 901")
tran = cir.create_setup("TR1", Setups.NexximTransient, TransientData=["1ns", "200ns"])
dc = cir.create_setup("DC1", Setups.NexximDC)
setup.add_sweep_points(sweep_variable="Freq", sweep_point=["1GHz", "2GHz"], units="GHz", override_existing_sweep=True)
setup.add_sweep_step(sweep_variable="Freq", start_point=1, end_point=10, step_size=0.1, units="GHz", override_existing_sweep=True)
setup.add_sweep_count(sweep_variable="Freq", start_point=1, end_point=10, count=901, units="GHz", count_type="Linear", override_existing_sweep=True)
setup.props / setup.update() / setup.analyze() / cir.analyze(setup=None)

parameters.name: setup_type
parameters.description: "NexximLNA", "NexximDC", "NexximTransient", "NexximQEye", "NexximVEye", "NexximAMI" (Setups enum constants).

parameters.name: Data
parameters.description: LNA frequency specification: "LINC start stop count", "LIN start stop step", "DEC start stop pointsPerDecade", or a list of points.

parameters.name: TransientData
parameters.description: [time_step, stop_time] for transient setups.

parameters.name: count_type
parameters.description: "Linear", "Decade", "Octave" for add_sweep_count.

tools.example:
lna = cir.create_setup("LNA1", setup_type="NexximLNA", Data="LINC 0.1GHz 20GHz 2000")
tr = cir.create_setup("TR1", setup_type="NexximTransient", TransientData=["5ps", "50ns"])
tr.props["TransientData"] = ["2ps", "100ns"]
tr.update()
cir.analyze("LNA1")
cir.post.create_report(["dB(S(P1,P1))", "dB(S(P2,P1))"], "LNA1")
tools.notes: Native: oModule = oDesign.GetModule("SimSetup"); oModule.AddLinearNetworkAnalysis(["NAME:SimSetup", "DataBlockID:=", 4, "OptionName:=", "(Default Options)", "AdditionalOptions:=", "", "AlterBlockName:=", "", "FilterText:=", "", "AnalysisEnabled:=", 1, ["NAME:SweepDefinition", "Variable:=", "F", "Data:=", "LINC 1GHz 10GHz 901", "OffsetF1:=", False, "Synchronize:=", 0], "Name:=", "LNA1", "LinearNetworkAnalysisSetupType:=", 0, ...]). Harmonic balance and envelope setups exist in the GUI but have no PyAEDT shortcut.

tools.name: circuit.push_excitations / push_time_excitations (Push Excitations to HFSS)
tools.description: Push the excitations computed in a circuit simulation back into the linked HFSS or 3D Layout design (Push Excitations): the port voltages/powers and phases of a linear (LNA) setup, optionally with a Thevenin equivalent, or the time-domain waveforms of a transient setup. After pushing, field plots and far fields in the EM design reflect the actual circuit drive (matching networks, amplifiers, terminations), which is how realistic field/SAR/radiation results are produced from a co-simulation.
tools.usage:
cir.push_excitations(instance, thevenin_calculation=False, setup="LinearFrequency")
cir.push_time_excitations(instance, start=0.0, stop=0.0, harmonics=100, window="Hamming", setup="NexximTransient")

parameters.name: instance
parameters.description: Name of the dynamically linked sub-circuit instance (e.g. "U1" or the component name).

parameters.name: thevenin_calculation
parameters.description: Push Thevenin equivalents (source + impedance) instead of incident powers.

parameters.name: setup
parameters.description: Circuit setup whose results are pushed.

parameters.name: start / stop / harmonics / window
parameters.description: Time window, number of harmonics and windowing for the transient push.

tools.example:
cir.analyze("LNA1")
cir.push_excitations("HFSS_Filter", thevenin_calculation=False, setup="LNA1")
hfss = Hfss(design="Filter")
hfss.post.create_fieldplot_surface("Trace", "Mag_Jsurf", intrinsics="2GHz", plot_name="J_pushed")
tools.notes: Native: oModule("Solutions")-side EditSources in the EM design receives the pushed values (they appear in Edit Sources with the circuit's magnitudes/phases). The Push Excitation from File extension does the same from a CSV without a circuit design.

tools.name: circuit.create_touchstone_report / export_touchstone / import_touchstone_solution / export_fullwave_spice / create_lna_schematic_from_snp / create_tdr_schematic_from_snp / create_ibis_schematic_from_snp
tools.description: Touchstone-centric circuit workflows: plot S-parameters of a Touchstone block with create_touchstone_report, export the circuit's own S-matrix, import a Touchstone file as a solution (for plotting/comparison without simulation), export a full-wave SPICE model (Network Data Explorer fitting), and one-call schematic generators that take an .sNp, build the schematic with sources/terminations/differential pairs and set up an LNA, TDR (transient) or IBIS analysis - the fastest route from an HFSS 3D Layout export to a TDR or eye study.
tools.usage:
cir.create_touchstone_report(name, curves, solution=None, variations=None, differential_pairs=False, subdesign_id=None)
cir.export_touchstone(setup=None, sweep=None, output_file=None, variations=None, variations_value=None, renormalization=False, impedance=None, gamma_impedance_comments=False)
cir.import_touchstone_solution(input_file, solution="Imported_Data")
cir.export_fullwave_spice(design=None, setup=None, is_solution_file=False, filename=None, passivity=False, causality=False, renormalize=False, impedance=50, error=0.5, poles=10000)
ok, diff, comm = cir.create_lna_schematic_from_snp(input_file, start_frequency=0, stop_frequency=30, auto_assign_diff_pairs=False, separation=".", pattern=None, design_name="LNA")
ok, diff, comm = cir.create_tdr_schematic_from_snp(input_file, probe_pins, probe_ref_pins=None, termination_pins=None, differential=True, rise_time=30, use_convolution=True, analyze=True, design_name="TDR")
ok, diff, comm = cir.create_ibis_schematic_from_snp(input_file, ibis_tx_file, tx_buffer_name, rx_buffer_name, ibis_rx_file=None, tx_pins=None, tx_refs=None, rx_pins=None, rx_refs=None, use_ibis_buffer=True, differential=True, bit_pattern=None, unit_interval=None, use_convolution=True, analyze=False, design_name="IBIS")

parameters.name: curves
parameters.description: Expressions such as ["dB(S(Port1,Port2))"] using the Touchstone block's port names.

parameters.name: probe_pins / termination_pins / rise_time
parameters.description: TDR: which ports are probed and terminated and the step rise time in ps.

parameters.name: auto_assign_diff_pairs / separation / pattern
parameters.description: Differential pair detection from port names built as component.pin.net.

parameters.name: passivity / causality / poles / error
parameters.description: Fitting options for the full-wave SPICE export.

tools.example:
cir = Circuit(version="2025.1", non_graphical=True)
ok, diffs, comms = cir.create_tdr_schematic_from_snp("C:/work/ddr.s8p", probe_pins=["U1.DQ0", "U1.DQ1"], termination_pins=["U2.DQ0", "U2.DQ1"],
                                                     differential=False, rise_time=35, analyze=True, design_name="TDR_DDR")
cir.post.create_report("TDRZ(U1.DQ0)", domain="Time")
cir.export_fullwave_spice(filename="C:/work/ddr_fw.sp", passivity=True, causality=True)
tools.notes: The generated schematics use Nexxim's TDR and IBIS-AMI components; results are in the Time domain (TDRZ, V probes) or as eye diagrams (post.reports_by_category.eye_diagram / ami). export_fullwave_spice needs the Network Data Explorer feature (NDE) license.

tools.name: Icepak (ansys.aedt.core.icepak.Icepak) / ipk.assign_em_losses (EM-to-thermal loss coupling)
tools.description: The Icepak application class opens or creates a thermal design in the same project, and assign_em_losses links it to a solved HFSS (or Maxwell/Q3D) design so the dielectric and conductor losses computed electromagnetically become volumetric/surface heat sources in the thermal solve, at a mapped frequency and with the source variables mapped. This is the RF-thermal co-simulation used for power amplifiers, filters, connectors and PCB self-heating; Icepak temperatures can be fed back through temperature-dependent materials.
tools.usage:
ipk = Icepak(project=None, design=None, solution_type=None, setup=None, version=None, non_graphical=False, new_desktop=False, close_on_exit=False, student_version=False, machine="", port=0, aedt_process_id=None, remove_lock=False)
bnd = ipk.assign_em_losses(assignment, design, setup, sweep, map_frequency=None, source_project_name=None, name=None, surface_objects=None,
                           parameters=None, force_source_solve=True, preserve_source_solution=True, loss_multiplier=1.0,
                           harmonic_loss_sweep_coupling=False, q3d_loss_type="DCVolOrACSurfLoss")
ipk.copy_solid_bodies_from(hfss, no_vacuum=True, no_pec=False)
ipk.create_setup(name="MySetupAuto", setup_type=None, **kwargs) / ipk.analyze()
ipk.assign_openings(air_faces) / ipk.assign_free_opening(...) / ipk.assign_stationary_wall_with_temperature(...)
ipk.assign_point_monitor(point_position, monitor_type="Temperature", monitor_name=None) / ipk.assign_surface_monitor(face_name, monitor_type="Temperature", monitor_name=None)
ipk.post.get_scalar_field_value("Temp", "Maximum", object_name="Chip")

parameters.name: assignment
parameters.description: Icepak objects that receive the losses (must correspond to objects in the source design, typically copied with copy_solid_bodies_from).

parameters.name: design / setup / sweep
parameters.description: Source HFSS design, setup and sweep ("LastAdaptive" or a sweep name).

parameters.name: map_frequency
parameters.description: Frequency at which losses are taken, e.g. "2.45GHz" (list allowed with harmonic coupling).

parameters.name: surface_objects
parameters.description: Objects whose losses are surface (finite-conductivity) losses rather than volume losses.

parameters.name: parameters
parameters.description: Dict mapping source design variables to values or Icepak variables.

parameters.name: loss_multiplier
parameters.description: Scale factor (or piecewise-linear dictionary versus time) applied to the mapped losses.

tools.example:
from ansys.aedt.core import Hfss, Icepak
hfss = Hfss(project="C:/work/pa.aedt", design="PA_RF")
hfss.analyze()
ipk = Icepak(design="PA_Thermal", solution_type="SteadyState")
ipk.copy_solid_bodies_from(hfss, no_vacuum=True, no_pec=False)
ipk.assign_em_losses(assignment=ipk.modeler.solid_names, design="PA_RF", setup="Setup1", sweep="LastAdaptive",
                     map_frequency="2.45GHz", surface_objects=hfss.get_all_conductors_names(), parameters={"Pin": "1W"})
ipk.assign_openings([f.id for f in ipk.modeler["Region"].faces])
ipk.create_setup("Thermal1")
ipk.analyze()
print(ipk.post.get_scalar_field_value("Temp", "Maximum", object_name="Trace"))
tools.notes: GUI: Icepak > Thermal > Assign > EM Loss. The EM losses are the HFSS volume loss density and surface loss density at the mapped frequency scaled by the excitation set in Edit Sources of the HFSS design; set the drive power there first. Two-way coupling (temperature feedback) uses hfss.modeler.set_objects_temperature / thermal modifiers.

tools.name: Maxwell3d / Maxwell2d (ansys.aedt.core.maxwell) constructors, solution types and key excitations
tools.description: The low-frequency EM applications in the same session: Maxwell3d and Maxwell2d designs with Magnetostatic, Eddy Current (AC Magnetic), Transient, Electrostatic, DC Conduction and Electric Transient solution types, with methods for current/voltage/coil/winding excitations, forces and torques, master/slave and insulating boundaries, eddy-effect control and Maxwell setups. Relevant to HFSS users for inductors, transformers, wireless-power coils, magnets and motor models that share geometry and materials with an HFSS project.
tools.usage:
m3d = Maxwell3d(project=None, design=None, solution_type=None, setup=None, version=None, non_graphical=False, new_desktop=False, ...)
m2d = Maxwell2d(project=None, design=None, solution_type=None, ...)      # 2D: XY or about Z (RZ) geometry mode
m3d.solution_type = "Magnetostatic" | "EddyCurrent" | "Transient" | "Electrostatic" | "DCConduction" | "ElectricTransient"
m3d.assign_current(assignment, amplitude=1, phase="0deg", solid=True, swap_direction=False, name=None)
m3d.assign_voltage(assignment, amplitude=1, name=None)
m3d.assign_coil(assignment, conductors_number=1, polarity="Positive", name=None)
m3d.assign_winding(assignment=None, winding_type="Current", is_solid=True, current=1, parallel_branches=1, phase=0, resistance=0, inductance=0, voltage=0, name=None)
m3d.add_winding_coils(assignment, coils)
m3d.assign_force(assignment, coordinate_system="Global", is_virtual=True, force_name=None) / m3d.assign_torque(...)
m3d.assign_master_slave(independent, dependent, u_vector_origin_coordinates_master, u_vector_pos_coordinates_master, ...)
m3d.assign_insulating(assignment, name=None) / m3d.eddy_effects_on(assignment, enable_eddy_effects=True, enable_displacement_current=True)
m3d.create_setup(name="MySetupAuto", setup_type=None, **kwargs)
m3d.assign_matrix(assignment, matrix_name=None, ...) / m3d.post.get_solution_data("Matrix1.L(Coil1,Coil1)")

parameters.name: solution_type
parameters.description: Set at construction or through the property; determines which excitations and setups are valid.

parameters.name: assign_winding / add_winding_coils
parameters.description: Winding (current, voltage or external circuit) that groups coil terminals; the standard excitation for transient and eddy designs.

parameters.name: assign_matrix
parameters.description: Inductance/capacitance matrix definition for magnetostatic/eddy/electrostatic parameter extraction.

tools.example:
from ansys.aedt.core import Maxwell3d
m3d = Maxwell3d(project=hfss.project_file, design="WPT_coil", solution_type="EddyCurrent", version="2025.1")
m3d.copy_solid_bodies_from(hfss, no_vacuum=False)
term = m3d.modeler.section("Coil", "XZ")
m3d.modeler.separate_bodies("Coil_Section1")
m3d.assign_coil("Coil_Section1", conductors_number=1, name="CoilTerminal")
m3d.assign_winding(winding_type="Current", current=1, name="Winding1")
m3d.add_winding_coils("Winding1", ["CoilTerminal"])
m3d.assign_matrix(["Winding1"], matrix_name="Matrix1")
setup = m3d.create_setup("Setup1", Frequency="100kHz", MaximumPasses=10)
m3d.analyze()
print(m3d.post.get_solution_data("Matrix1.L(Winding1,Winding1)").primary_sweep_values)
tools.notes: Native design type names for oProject.InsertDesign: "Maxwell 3D", "Maxwell 2D" with solution types "Magnetostatic", "EddyCurrent", "Transient", "Electrostatic", "DCConduction". Maxwell has its own mesh (m3d.mesh) with assign_length_mesh and cylindrical gap operations, and a MaxwellCircuit class for external circuit excitations.

tools.name: Q3d / Q2d (ansys.aedt.core.q3d) constructors, nets, sources/sinks, matrices and RLGC export
tools.description: Q3D Extractor and 2D Extractor application classes for quasi-static RLCG extraction: automatic net identification from conductor connectivity, assignment of sources and sinks on faces (or objects), creation of setups (DC RL, AC RL, CG), reduced matrices (series/parallel/ground operations), and export of the matrices or equivalent circuits (SPICE, Touchstone-like RLGC). HFSS users combine Q3D for package/connector parasitics at low frequency with HFSS for the high-frequency behaviour, and Circuit links both.
tools.usage:
q3d = Q3d(project=None, design=None, solution_type=None, setup=None, version=None, non_graphical=False, new_desktop=False, ...)
q2d = Q2d(project=None, design=None, ...)
q3d.auto_identify_nets()
q3d.assign_net(assignment, net_name=None, net_type=None)        # net_type "Signal", "Ground", "Floating"
q3d.source(assignment=None, direction=0, name=None, net_name=None, terminal_type="voltage")
q3d.sink(assignment=None, direction=0, name=None, net_name=None, terminal_type="voltage")
q3d.create_setup(name="MySetupAuto", setup_type=None, **kwargs)      # props: AdaptiveFreq, DC/AC/CG enable, MaxPass, MinPass, PercentError
q3d.insert_reduced_matrix(operation_name, assignment=None, reduced_matrix=None, new_net_name=None, new_source=None, new_sink=None)
q3d.export_matrix_data(file_name, problem_type=None, solution=None, variations=None, matrix_type="Maxwell", ...)
q3d.export_equivalent_circuit(output_file, setup=None, sweep=None, variations=None, matrix=None, coupling_limit_type=None, ...)
q3d.get_mutual_coupling(source1=None, sink1=None, source2=None, sink2=None, calculation="ACL")
q3d.nets / q3d.net_sources(net) / q3d.net_sinks(net) / q3d.get_all_sources()

parameters.name: assignment / direction
parameters.description: Object or face(s) for the terminal; direction hfss.AxisDir-style when an object is given.

parameters.name: terminal_type
parameters.description: "voltage" or "current" terminal definition.

parameters.name: problem_type
parameters.description: "C", "AC RL", "DC RL" (or combinations) for export_matrix_data.

parameters.name: operation_name
parameters.description: Reduced-matrix operation: "Join Series", "Join Parallel", "Float Net", "Ground Net", "Return Path", "Change Freq".

tools.example:
from ansys.aedt.core import Q3d
q3d = Q3d(project="C:/work/package.aedt", design="Leadframe", version="2025.1")
q3d.modeler.import_3d_cad("C:/cad/leadframe.step")
q3d.auto_identify_nets()
src = q3d.source("Pin1", direction=q3d.AxisDir.ZNeg, name="Src1")
snk = q3d.sink("Pin1", direction=q3d.AxisDir.ZPos, name="Snk1")
setup = q3d.create_setup("Setup1", AdaptiveFreq="1GHz")
q3d.analyze()

tools.notes: Native design names: "Q3D Extractor" and "2D Extractor". Q3D results plug into Circuit via schematic.add_q3d_rlgc / add_subcircuit_dynamic_link, and into Icepak via assign_em_losses with q3d_loss_type.

tools.name: Emit / Mechanical / TwinBuilder / Rmxprt / MaxwellCircuit / FilterSolutions (other AEDT application classes)
tools.description: The remaining application classes reachable from the same PyAEDT session: Emit for RF co-site interference and spectrum analysis (radios, antennas, coupling from HFSS results, with emit.results and revision/interference APIs), Mechanical for structural/thermal FEA designs inside AEDT (with EM loss and temperature links), TwinBuilder for system simulation schematics, Rmxprt for electric-machine templates that generate Maxwell designs, MaxwellCircuit for external circuits coupled to Maxwell transient, and FilterSolutions for lumped/distributed filter synthesis that can export to HFSS/Circuit. All share the constructor signature and the project/design/variable/report infrastructure of Hfss.
tools.usage:
from ansys.aedt.core import Emit, Mechanical, TwinBuilder, Rmxprt, MaxwellCircuit, FilterSolutions
emit = Emit(project=None, design=None, solution_type=None, setup=None, version=None, non_graphical=False, new_desktop=False, ...)
mech = Mechanical(project=None, design=None, solution_type=None, ...)      # "Thermal", "Structural", "Modal"
tb = TwinBuilder(project=None, design=None, solution_type=None, ...)
rmx = Rmxprt(project=None, design=None, solution_type=None, model_units=None, ...)
fs = FilterSolutions(version=None, implementation_type=None)
emit.modeler.components.create_radio_antenna(radio_type, radio_name=None, antenna_name=None, ...) / emit.results / emit.analyze()
mech.assign_em_losses(design, setup, sweep, map_frequency, surface_objects=None, source_project_name=None, parameters=None, assignment=None)
mech.assign_thermal_map(...) / mech.assign_uniform_convection(...) / mech.assign_fixed_support(...)

parameters.name: Emit
parameters.description: Designs contain radios, antennas and couplings; the EMIT API (emit.results.get_revision, interference_type_classification) supports automated interference matrices; the Interference Classification extension wraps it.

parameters.name: Mechanical
parameters.description: Structural or thermal analysis of HFSS geometry; EM losses from HFSS and temperatures from Icepak are linked like in Icepak.

parameters.name: TwinBuilder
parameters.description: System-level schematic with modeler.schematic components and TwinBuilder setups (TR, AC, DC); can import Q3D/Maxwell reduced-order models.

parameters.name: Rmxprt
parameters.description: Machine templates (RMxprt design types) and rmx.create_maxwell_design(...) to export to Maxwell 2D/3D.

parameters.name: FilterSolutions
parameters.description: Standalone filter synthesis API (lumped or distributed); design export to AEDT projects.

tools.example:
from ansys.aedt.core import Emit, Mechanical
emit = Emit(project="C:/work/cosite.aedt", design="CoSite", version="2025.1")
radio, ant = emit.modeler.components.create_radio_antenna("Bluetooth Low Energy (LE)", radio_name="BLE", antenna_name="BLE_Ant")
rev = emit.results.analyze()
print(emit.results.get_revision().get_interference_type_classification if hasattr(emit.results.get_revision(), 'get_interference_type_classification') else rev)

mech = Mechanical(project=hfss.project_file, design="Structural", solution_type="Structural")
mech.copy_solid_bodies_from(hfss, no_vacuum=True, no_pec=False)
mech.assign_em_losses(design="PA_RF", setup="Setup1", sweep="LastAdaptive", map_frequency="2.45GHz", assignment=mech.modeler.solid_names)
tools.notes: Native design type strings for oProject.InsertDesign: "EMIT", "Mechanical", "Twin Builder", "RMxprt", "Maxwell Circuit", "Icepak", "Circuit Design", "HFSS 3D Layout Design", "Q3D Extractor", "2D Extractor", "Maxwell 3D", "Maxwell 2D". EMIT requires its own license and 2023 R2+ for the results API.

tools.name: h3d.set_differential_pair / get_differential_pairs / load_diff_pairs_from_file / save_diff_pairs_to_file (3D Layout)
tools.description: Differential pair definitions in a layout design: create pairs from two ports with differential/common mode names and reference impedances, list the defined pairs, and load or save pair definitions from/to a text file so the same pairs are reused across cutouts and design versions. Mixed-mode quantities (S(Diff1,Diff1), TDR differential) become available in reports and Touchstone export once pairs exist.
tools.usage:
h3d.set_differential_pair(assignment, reference, common_mode=None, differential_mode=None, common_reference=25, differential_reference=100, active=True, matched=False)
h3d.get_differential_pairs()
h3d.load_diff_pairs_from_file(input_file)
h3d.save_diff_pairs_to_file(output_file)

parameters.name: assignment / reference
parameters.description: Positive and negative port names.

parameters.name: differential_mode / common_mode
parameters.description: Mode names (auto-generated when None).

parameters.name: differential_reference / common_reference
parameters.description: Reference impedances in ohms.

parameters.name: input_file / output_file
parameters.description: Text file with one pair definition per line (the format the Differential Pairs dialog exports).

tools.example:
ports = h3d.port_list
h3d.set_differential_pair("U1.DQS_P", "U1.DQS_N", differential_mode="DQS_U1", common_mode="DQS_U1_C", differential_reference=100)
h3d.set_differential_pair("U2.DQS_P", "U2.DQS_N", differential_mode="DQS_U2", common_mode="DQS_U2_C")
print(h3d.get_differential_pairs())
h3d.save_diff_pairs_to_file("C:/work/diffpairs.txt")
h3d.post.create_report("dB(S(DQS_U1,DQS_U2))", context="Differential Pairs")
tools.notes: PyEDB's edb.differential_pairs.auto_identify defines pairs at the net level before ports exist; the layout-level pairs here are port-based. Circuit has the same four methods for schematic designs.

tools.name: h3d.modeler.place_3d_component / components_3d / dissolve_component / create_component_on_pins
tools.description: 3D components inside a layout: place an HFSS .a3dcomp (a connector, an antenna, a package model) on the board at a position and layer with the placement tolerance and optional variable mapping, list the placed 3D components, dissolve a component into its primitives, and build a new layout component from a set of pins (padstack instances). This is how connectors and modules are attached to a board for a combined HFSS 3D Layout solve.
tools.usage:
comp = h3d.modeler.place_3d_component(component_path, number_of_terminals=1, placement_layer=None, component_name=None, pos_x=0, pos_y=0, create_ports=True, is_boundary=False)
h3d.modeler.components_3d
h3d.dissolve_component(component)
h3d.modeler.create_component_on_pins(pins, definition_name=None, component_name=None)
h3d.modeler.import_cadence_brd(input_file, output_dir=None, ...) / h3d.modeler.import_ipc2581(input_file, ...)

parameters.name: component_path
parameters.description: Path to the .a3dcomp (or an Encrypted/layout component .aedbcomp).

parameters.name: number_of_terminals
parameters.description: Number of port terminals the component exposes to the layout.

parameters.name: placement_layer / pos_x / pos_y
parameters.description: Layer and position of the component origin in layout units.

parameters.name: create_ports / is_boundary
parameters.description: Create ports on the component terminals; treat the component as a boundary (e.g. an absorber block).

tools.example:
conn = h3d.modeler.place_3d_component("C:/lib/sma_edge.a3dcomp", number_of_terminals=1, placement_layer="TOP", component_name="SMA1", pos_x="0mm", pos_y="0mm", create_ports=True)
print(h3d.modeler.components_3d.keys(), h3d.port_list)
h3d.dissolve_component("SMA1")
tools.notes: GUI: Layout > Place 3D Component (HFSS 3D Layout supports 3D components from 2020 R1) and Layout Components (.aedbcomp, a layout exported as a component with edb.export_layout_component). Terminal pads must coincide with layout geometry on the placement layer.
